title: Energy hard to hold?
caption: Energy hard to hold? Today looks calm and steady up there—some room to recoup, even if you are not feeling better yet. Pick one must-do and finish it, then take a short movement break or a minute of slow breaths before the next thing.
snapshot: Geomagnetic activity is quiet. Solar wind is running at typical speeds with a slight southward tilt. No solar flares were recorded. One CME was observed with no indication of Earth impact.
affects: Low energy may still show up for some, but steadier conditions can help you spend it more cleanly. People often find one or two tasks are manageable without as much scatter. Short rests between efforts support staying steady.
playbook:
- Choose one must-do and finish it
- Take a short movement or breathing break
- Drink water before reaching for more caffeine
- Keep lighting soft to reduce load
- Check local weather, wind, and allergens

fb.caption:
Energy hard to hold? Today is running calmer overhead—magnetic conditions look settled and the solar wind isn’t throwing surprises—so effort may land a bit more cleanly, even if you are not feeling better yet. steadier footing without a guaranteed energy bump.

Aim for one real must‑do and see it all the way through, then stand up for a minute of easy movement or take six slow breaths before starting the next thing. That quick reset helps your nervous system downshift and keeps focus from smearing across tasks. Sip water before reaching for extra caffeine to avoid a late slump, and soften bright lighting to lower strain. If allergies or local wind kick up where you are, factor that into your pace.
